clue.text: Slip back into the gun room

indicators.note: into says the turned slip goes inside the word for a gun

parts.note: GAT is old slang for a gun or pistol

indicators.note: back tells us the word for a slip is to be read from right to left

parts.note: to slip is to make a mistake, to err

explanation.surface: Someone slips back into the gun room of a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' looks like a noun for a petticoat or a fall, but it is the verb, to make a mistake. GAT is old American gangster slang for a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: A garret is an attic room under the roof, so it is one kind of room.

clue.text: A way through on foot

definitions.meaning: a curved opening you can walk under, as in a gateway in a wall
the raised curve of the sole between heel and ball

explanation.surface: A footpath through somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a curved structure spanning a passage and the curved underside of the foot.

clue.text: Measuring device for cats and dogs?

definitions.text: Measuring device for cats and dogs?

parts.words: Measuring device for cats and dogs?
parts.note: sounds like a pet scale, but raining cats and dogs means pouring, so the device measures downpours

explanation.definitionFit: Raining cats and dogs is an idiom for heavy rainfall, which this instrument records.

clue.text: Take down in an attempt to reach agreement

indicators.note: in tells us the word for taking down goes inside the word for an attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to take down food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get a deal by making notes in a negotiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take down' suggests writing a note, but here it means swallowing food.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between states.

clue.text: They don't believe in free speech

definitions.text: They don't believe in free speech

parts.words: They don't believe in free speech
parts.note: reads like censors, but describes people who shout down a speaker rather than let them talk unchallenged

explanation.definitionFit: Hecklers interrupt public speakers with jeers, refusing them an unimpeded hearing.

clue.text: Strike teacher, get punishment and feature in the newspaper

parts.note: to strike is to hit
the head is the head teacher of a school
lines are a school punishment: writing out a sentence many times

explanation.surface: A pupil who hits a teacher ends up punished and makes the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines, a traditional British school punishment, means copying out the same sentence over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the headlines is an idiom for becoming front-page news.

clue.text: Vehicle owner may be distressed

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters of owner may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Owning a car can be stressful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' is a loose anagram signal: the owner's letters may be rearranged. The car owner's letters together also spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Careworn means worn down by worry, showing strain or distress.

clue.text: One of the Stones that rocks?

definitions.text: One of the Stones that rocks?

parts.words: One of the Stones that rocks?
parts.note: reads as a member of the Rolling Stones band, but means a balanced boulder that rocks when pushed

explanation.definitionFit: A logan, or logan stone, is a large balanced stone that rocks at a touch, found in Cornwall.

clue.text: Odd messengers craftily dodging duty

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the people who do this

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
runners carry messages

explanation.surface: Strange couriers slyly avoid their obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty' looks like an obligation, but it is customs duty on liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Smugglers of alcohol evade the customs tax, so they are the people craftily dodging duty.

clue.text: Mishap caused by stress — I'd go into it

indicators.note: go into it says the short word goes inside the word for stress

parts.note: accent is stress laid on a syllable
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Stress led to a blunder, and I'll explain why.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unfortunate event, a mishap.

clue.text: Émigré beaten up by the authorities

indicators.note: beaten up suggests the letters of the exile are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An exile is assaulted by the state's police.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is the governing power, the authorities in charge of a state.

clue.text: Receive notice of termination and become agitated

definitions.meaning: a wind-up is the winding up or ending of something, so to receive it is to be told it is over
an idiom for becoming frightened or nervous

explanation.surface: Someone gets the sack and gets upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to take fright, and a wind-up is an ending or termination.

clue.text: Local inn around Tyneside may provide Italian dish

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: A pub in Newcastle might serve pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges the letters of LOCAL INN together with NE. Tyneside is the area around Newcastle in North East England; 'may provide' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannelloni is an Italian dish of tubes of pasta filled and baked.

clue.text: Bill gets university ban

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab

explanation.surface: A bill gets the university to impose a prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, a prohibition or ban.

clue.text: Policy that's uncompromising is almost a shame

indicators.note: almost means the phrase stops short of its final letter

parts.note: hard lines is British slang for bad luck, a shame

explanation.surface: An inflexible policy is nearly a pity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of HARD LINES, a British expression of sympathy meaning bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard line is a firm, unyielding policy or stance.

clue.text: Former habit of night workers

parts.note: late means former, as in the late president
a habit is a garment, and a shift is a simple dress

explanation.surface: Night workers used to have a regular custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' looks like a routine, but it is clothing, a shift dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The late shift is the group of employees working through the night.

clue.text: Ring for support after shipwreck

parts.note: sounds like phoning for help, but is a buoyant ring that holds a survivor up in the water

explanation.definitionFit: A buoyant ring thrown to a person in the water keeps them afloat.

clue.text: Very good article for cake decoration

parts.note: angelic means very good, like an angel
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A very fine item for decorating a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Candied stalks of the herb are used as green decoration on cakes.

clue.text: Exhaust seen on an American car

definitions.meaning: to exhaust is to wear out or fatigue
the US spelling of the rubber wheel covering the British spell with a y

explanation.surface: An exhaust pipe spotted on a US car.
explanation.definitionFit: To tire is to exhaust, and Americans spell the wheel's rubber covering this way.

clue.text: Flower book

definitions.meaning: a plant that lives for only one year
a yearbook, or a children's book published once a year

explanation.surface: A book about flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a plant completing its life in one year, and also a yearly publication.

clue.text: Changes of gear may depend on them

definitions.text: Changes of gear may depend on them

parts.words: Changes of gear may depend on them
parts.note: reads as car gearboxes, but gear here is clothing hung up to dry on lines

explanation.definitionFit: Clothes hang from these lines, and gear is informal for clothing.

clue.text: It's quite rough and ready as a rule

definitions.text: It's quite rough and ready as a rule

parts.words: It's quite rough and ready as a rule
parts.note: a rule of ... is a rough and ready method, so this digit is the rough measure

explanation.definitionFit: A rule of thumb is an approximate practical guideline, named after the digit used for rough measuring.

clue.text: A slap on the wrist

definitions.meaning: a light blow with the hand
the end of a sleeve that wraps around the wrist

explanation.surface: A mild punishment, like a slap on the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuff is a blow with the open hand and also the band of a sleeve at the wrist.

clue.text: Sound content of a book

definitions.meaning: the loudness of a sound, how much noise there is
a single book, especially one of a set

explanation.surface: What a book is about, in terms of its words.
explanation.definitionFit: Volume is the amount of sound, and also one book of a series.

clue.text: Just a shell until USA converted it into a nuclear sub

definitions.text: Just a shell until USA converted it into a nuclear sub

indicators.note: converted suggests the letters are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A mere shell until the US Navy turned it into a nuclear submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges UNTIL and USA. The shellfish gave its name to the first US nuclear submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: The nautilus is a sea creature with a spiral shell, and USS Nautilus was the first nuclear submarine.

clue.text: Expires without help for disease

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for expires surrounds the other

parts.note: to expire is to die
to abet is to help

explanation.surface: Someone dies with no help available for an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but has its old sense of outside, so one word encloses the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabetes is a disease affecting the body's control of blood sugar.

clue.text: Released and shot

definitions.meaning: freed from a penalty or duty
fired, as a gun or firework is discharged

explanation.surface: A prisoner freed and then shot.
explanation.definitionFit: To let off is to release from punishment, and also to fire a gun or set off a firework.
